title: Weighing yourself in an accelerating lift
caption: To accelerate upward at 2.0 m s⁻² the scales must push up harder than the weight: R = m(g + a) = 60 × 11.8 = 708 N, against a weight of 588 N. The scales read the push, 708 N, as if the mass were 72.2 kg.
alt: Free-body diagram of a person in a lift: weight 588 newtons down, normal force 708 newtons up, net 120 newtons up.
description: Normal force from the scales: R, up.
Newton's second law upward: R − 588 = 60 × 2, so R = 708 N.
